Testimony of the Office of Aging and Disability Services
Maine Department of Health and Human Services
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
In support of LD 2021, An Act to Add an Online Option for Reporting ofSuspected Abuse,
Neglect and Exploitation ofAdults
Sponsor: Representative Meyer Hearing Date: January 14, 2026
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Health and Human Services, my name is Betsy Hopkins, and I serve as the Director Within the Office of Aging and Disability Services (OADS) in the Maine Department of Health and Human Services. I am here today to testify in support of LD 2021, An Act to Add an Online Option for
Reporting ofSuspected Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation ofAdults.
Under current law, mandated reporters are required to report suspected abuse, neglect, or
exploitation (ANE) of adults to the Department by telephone. LD 2021 would add an online
reporting option for mandated reporters, providing an additional method for submitting reports. This change would bring Maine statute into alignment with federal regulations finalized in June 2024, which require states to offer at least two methods for reporting, one of which must be
online.
The Office of Aging and Disability Services' Adult Protective Services Intake Unit already allows members of the public who are not mandated reporters to submit reports of abuse,
neglect, or exploitation through an online portal. LD 2021 would clarify and update our statutory framework to allow mandated reporters to also use this existing APS intake system.
Maine has until May of 2028 to comply with the APS Federal Law. LD 2021 addresses one
component of that federal law and provides mandated reporters with an additional, accessible
option for reporting concerns. For these reasons, I support LD 2021.
Thank you for your time and attention. I would be happy to answer any questions and remain available for the work session

Dear Representative Meyer and Members of the Health and Human Services Committee,
Thankyou for the opportunity to submit testimony on LD 2021 , An Act to Add an Online Option for
Reporting ofSuspected Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation ofAdults.
I understand that this bill is necessaryto bring Maine into compliance with federal regulations requiring at least two reporting methods, including an online option. For that reason, l agree that this legislation
must move forward.
However, my concern is that the bill, as written, adds a new intake mechanism without adding a
gatekeeper, clear operational standards, or accountability measures. DHHS is effectively being asked to
build and operate a critical system at the same time, without legislative guardrails.
Allowing online reporting will almost certainly increase report volume. That is not inherently bad, but without clear triage rules, response timelines, or confirmation protocols, it creates real risk. An online submission can easily give reporters a false sense of securitythat a report has been received, reviewed,
and acted upon, when in reality it may be sitting in a queue in an already overburdened system.
The bill does not currently address:
- How quickly online reports must be reviewed by a human ~ How urgent cases will be identified and prioritized
- Whether reporters will receive confirmation and guidance
~ How DHHS will manage increased volume without additional capacity - How the Legislature or public will know whether the system is working
This is not a technology issue; it is a systems issue. Intake without triage is not protection. Reporting without response is not safety.
l respectfully urge the Committee to advance LD 2021 with safeguards that ensure this modernization does not unintentionally increase riskto vulnerable adults. Reasonable additions could include:
- Clear language that online reporting does not replace emergency reporting requirements - Required confirmation to reporters, including next steps and when to call immediately
- Defined timelines for human review and triage of online submissions
1

- Internal prioritization standards for high-risk reports
~ Aggregate public reporting on volume, response times, and outcomes These additions would not slow implementation. They would strengthen it. Modernizing reporting mechanisms is appropriate and necessary. But modernization without oversight capacity planning, and accountability places both reporters and vulnerable adults at risk.
For these reasons, I support LD 2021 with amendments that ensure the system has a gatekeeper, not
just a front door.
Thankyou foryourtime and consideration.
Respectfully,

Testimony of Laura Cordes
LD 2021: An Act to Add an Online Option for Reporting of Suspected Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of Adults
Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services January 14, 2026
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony in support of LD 2021 which would add an online option for mandated reporters to utilize when reporting suspected abuse, neglect, and exploitation of adults to Adult Protective Services (APS).
MACSP represents nearly 100 community-based agencies across Maine that deliver person-centered educational, vocational, residential, and community supports, as well as specialized care, to children and adults with intellectual disabilities, autism spectrum disorder, and brain injuries. Our members support thousands of Mainers of all ages to live safely, with dignity, and as fully integrated members of their communities.
Staff delivering MaineCare services for individuals with intellectual disabilities and brain injuries are mandated reporters under Maine law. Currently, these mandated reporters are limited to making reports to APS by telephone only. While Maine already maintains an APS online reporting tool, that system is available only to non-mandated reporters, creating an unnecessary and inequitable distinction in access to reporting options.
Expanding online reporting access to mandated reporters would meaningfully improve the reporting system. Online reporting can increase accessibility and timeliness, particularly in settings where making a phone call is challenging, and may help ensure a clear and accurate record of when and how a report was made.
Research consistently shows that people with disabilities experience higher rates of abuse, neglect, and exploitation and that these incidents are often underreported by the individuals themselves. Direct support professionals and other frontline staff work closely with the individuals they support, as well as with family members and friends, and other support staff, and are often among the first to identify concerns or receive disclosures of harm. When concerns arise, reporting mechanisms must be accessible, responsive, and reliable.
LD 2021 would bring Maine law into alignment with federal regulations adopted in June 2024, which require states to maintain at least two methods for reporting abuse, neglect, and exploitation, including

one online option. This bill represents a practical and necessary update that builds on existing infrastructure rather than creating a new system. By expanding access to online reporting for mandated reporters, LD 2021 strengthens protections for adults who are vulnerable to abuse, neglect, or exploitation and supports timely intervention when concerns arise. For these reasons, MACSP urges the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on LD 2021. Thank you for your consideration. Please reach out with questions or requests for additional information. Respectfully submitted, Laura Cordes Executive Director laura.cordes@meacsp.org

Senator Ingwersen and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human
Services. As you know, I am Representative Michele Meyer, and I am here to present LD 2021,
An Act to Add an Online Option for Reporting of Suspected Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation of Adults, on behalf of the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS).
This is a bill brought forth by the Office of Aging and Disability Services and would ensure compliance with federal regulations that became law in June 2024. Currently, Maine law states: "Reports regarding abuse, neglect, or exploitation must be made immediately by telephone to the department and must be followed by a written report within 48 hours if requested by the
department." The new Adult Protective Services (APS) Federal Law requires that states allow for
at least two methods of reporting, one of which must be online.
This simple change will bring the State of Maine into compliance with federal law and provide
an additional avenue for reports to be made. I hope we can all agree that those are two very good
reasons to support this bill.
The new Director of the Office of Aging and Disability Services, Betsy Hopkins, will provide
additional information regarding existing online capabilities following my testimony. I ask that
you save your questions for her. Thank you for your time.
